title: Remove negative numbers
description: The function remove_negatives returns the list without negative numbers. The other numbers keep their order. Zero is not a negative number.
bug_description: The call numbers.remove(number) deletes an element from the same list the for loop is iterating over. The remaining elements shift left, so the loop skips the element right after the removed one. When two negative numbers are next to each other, the second one stays in the result: [-1, -2, 3] returns [-2, 3] instead of [3].
hints_json: Does the function work for every order of numbers in the list, or only for some?
What does the function return for the list [-1, -2, 3], where two negative numbers are next to each other?
Look at what happens to the list the loop is iterating over when numbers.remove is called.
fallback_feedback: The bug is the call numbers.remove(number) inside a loop that iterates over the same list. When an element is removed, the others shift left and the loop skips the next element, so the second of two consecutive negative numbers stays in the result. Build the result in a new list instead of removing items from the list the loop is iterating over.
